cards.claim: Stoichiometry is the calculation of the masses (and sometimes volumes) of reactants and products in a chemical reaction.
cards.quote: Stoichiometry, thus, deals with the calculation of masses (sometimes volumes also) of the reactants and the products involved in a chemical reaction.

cards.claim: The coefficients in a balanced equation are stoichiometric coefficients; they give the numbers of molecules, and equally of moles, that react or form.
cards.quote: The coefficients 2 for O 2 and H 2O are called stoichiometric coefficients. Similarly the coefficient for CH4 and CO2 is one in each case. They represent the number of molecules (and moles as well) taking part in the reaction or formed in the reaction.

cards.claim: For CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O, the mole ratio 1:2:1:2 corresponds to 16 g of CH4 reacting with 2 × 32 g of O2 to give 44 g of CO2 and 2 × 18 g of H2O.
cards.quote: 16 g of CH 4 (g) reacts with 2×32 g of O 2 (g) to give 44 g of CO 2 (g) and 2×18 g of H2O (g).

cards.claim: Stoichiometric ratios can be read only from a balanced equation, which has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides, as the law of conservation of mass requires.
cards.quote: According to the law of conservation of mass, a balanced chemical equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides of the equation.

cards.claim: NCERT Problem 1.3: to find the mass of water from 16 g of methane, note that 16 g CH4 is one mole and 1 mol CH4 gives 2 mol H2O (36 g).
cards.quote: Calculate the amount of water (g) produced by the combustion of 16 g of methane.

cards.claim: NCERT Problem 1.4 result: since 1 mol CO2 comes from 1 mol CH4, producing 22 g (0.5 mol) of CO2 requires 0.5 mol of CH4.
cards.quote: Hence, 0.5 mol CO 2 (g) would be obtained from 0.5 mol CH4 (g) or 0.5 mol of CH4 (g) would be required to produce 22 g CO2 (g).

cards.claim: An equation is balanced by changing coefficients only; the subscripts in the formulas of reactants and products must never be changed.
cards.quote: Always remember that subscripts in formulas of reactants and products cannot be changed to balance an equation.

cards.claim: NCERT Exemplar 1.31 (short answer): Zn + 2HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2; what volume of H2 at STP is liberated when 32.65 g of zinc reacts (1 mol gas = 22.7 L at STP; Zn = 65.3 u)?
cards.quote: Hydrogen gas is prepared in the laboratory by reacting dilute HCl with granulated zinc. Following reaction takes place. Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2 Calculate the volume of hydrogen gas liberated at STP when 32.65 g of zinc reacts with HCl. 1 mol of a gas occupies 22.7 L volume at STP; atomic mass of Zn = 65.3 u.

cards.quote: From the equation, 63.5 g of zinc liberates 22.7 litre of hydrogen. So 32.65 g of zinc will liberate 222.7 L H32.65 g Zn × 65.3 g Zn = 22.7 L = 11.35 L2

cards.claim: NCERT Exemplar 1.41 (assertion-reason): Assertion - combustion of 16 g of methane gives 18 g of water; Reason - in the combustion of methane, water is one of the products.
cards.quote: Assertion (A) : Combustion of 16 g of methane gives 18 g of water. Reason (R) : In the combustion of methane, water is one of the products. (i) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A. (ii) A is true but R is false. (iii) A is false but R is true. (iv) Both A and R are false.
